description: Laboratory experiments are based upon the corresponding theory course EEPC-209. An updated list of experiments is floated by the course coordinator before the beginning of each semester.
outcomes: Evaluate the operation and design of transmission lines.
Apply numerical techniques for load flow calculations.
Analyze different faults using the Z-bus building algorithm and the stability of a power system.
Understand the operation of circuit breakers and high voltage generation techniques.
experiments: Determine the ABCD parameters of a transmission line and calculate its regulation and efficiency.
Formulate the bus admittance matrix using graph theory and a direct building algorithm considering phase shifters and transformers.
Perform load flow analysis using the Gauss-Seidel method.
Perform load flow analysis using the Newton-Raphson method and the fast decoupled technique.
Perform Z-bus formation and symmetrical fault analysis.
Perform unsymmetrical fault analysis using the Z-bus technique.
Simulate the Marx circuit for impulse generation.
Demonstrate the Marx circuit for switching and lightning impulse generation.
Study the breakdown of air using high voltage AC with different electrode geometries.
Study the operation of an MCCB and an air circuit breaker.
Perform stability analysis using the Runge-Kutta method.
Perform a dielectric test on transformer oil.
Design a transmission line using given specifications as an individual design project.
